question: What are the normal hours of work of an employee in the Philippines?
expected_answer: The normal hours of work shall not exceed eight hours a day under Labor Code Art. 83.

evidence.quote: The normal hours of work of any employee shall not exceed eight (8) hours a day.

question: What is the night shift differential and which hours does it cover?
expected_answer: Not less than 10% of the regular wage for each hour worked between 10 in the evening and 6 in the morning, under Labor Code Art. 86.

evidence.quote: not less than ten percent (10%) of his regular wage for each hour of work performed between ten o’clock in the evening and six o’clock in the morning

question: How much overtime pay is due for work beyond eight hours, on an ordinary day and on a holiday or rest day?
expected_answer: On an ordinary day, the regular wage plus at least 25%. On a holiday or rest day, the rate of the first eight hours plus at least 30%. See Labor Code Art. 87.

evidence.quote: an additional compensation equivalent to his regular wage plus at least twenty-five percent (25%) thereof
the rate of the first eight hours on a holiday or rest day plus at least thirty percent (30%) thereof

key_points.label: 30 percent on a holiday or rest day

question: How long must the meal period be for regular meals?
expected_answer: Not less than 60 minutes of time-off, under Labor Code Art. 85.

evidence.quote: not less than sixty (60) minutes time-off for their regular meals

question: What premium is due for work on a scheduled rest day, and for work on a special holiday that falls on the scheduled rest day?
expected_answer: At least 30% of the regular wage for a scheduled rest day, and at least 50% where special holiday work falls on the scheduled rest day, under Labor Code Art. 93.

evidence.quote: he shall be paid an additional compensation of at least thirty percent (30%) of his regular wage
he shall be entitled to an additional compensation of at least fifty per cent (50%) of his regular wage

key_points.label: 50 percent on a special holiday on a rest day

question: How much must an employee be paid for working on a regular holiday?
expected_answer: Twice the regular rate, under Labor Code Art. 94(b).

evidence.quote: such employee shall be paid a compensation equivalent to twice his regular rate

question: Which establishments are exempt from paying the regular daily wage during regular holidays?
expected_answer: Retail and service establishments regularly employing less than ten workers, under Labor Code Art. 94(a).

evidence.quote: except in retail and service establishments regularly employing less than ten (10) workers

question: How often must wages be paid?
expected_answer: At least once every two weeks or twice a month, at intervals not exceeding 16 days, under Labor Code Art. 103.

evidence.quote: Wages shall be paid at least once every two (2) weeks or twice a month at intervals not exceeding sixteen (16) days.

key_points.label: twice a month or every two weeks

question: When may an employer deduct from an employee's wages?
expected_answer: Only where the worker is insured with consent and the deduction recompenses the premium, for union dues where check-off is recognized or authorized, and where authorized by law or by regulations of the Secretary of Labor and Employment, under Labor Code Art. 113.

evidence.quote: In cases where the worker is insured with his consent by the employer
For union dues
In cases where the employer is authorized by law or regulations issued by the Secretary of Labor and Employment

question: Can undertime on one day be offset by overtime on another day?
expected_answer: No. Undertime on any particular day shall not be offset by overtime on any other day, under Labor Code Art. 88.

evidence.quote: Undertime work on any particular day shall not be offset by overtime work on any other day.

question: Who is entitled to service incentive leave and how long is it?
expected_answer: Every employee who has rendered at least one year of service is entitled to five days of leave with pay a year, under Labor Code Art. 95.

evidence.quote: Every employee who has rendered at least one year of service shall be entitled to a yearly service incentive leave of five days with pay.

question: Which employees are not covered by service incentive leave?
expected_answer: Those already enjoying the benefit, those with vacation leave with pay of at least five days, those in establishments regularly employing less than ten employees, and those in establishments exempted by the Secretary of Labor and Employment, under Labor Code Art. 95.

evidence.quote: those enjoying vacation leave with pay of at least five days and those employed in establishments regularly employing less than ten employees

key_points.label: vacation leave of at least five days
establishments with less than ten employees

question: At what age may an employee retire when there is no retirement plan, and how is retirement pay computed?
expected_answer: Without a plan, an employee aged 60 or more, up to the compulsory retirement age of 65, who has served at least five years may retire and receives at least one-half month salary for every year of service, under Labor Code Art. 302.

evidence.quote: an employee upon reaching the age of sixty (60) years or more, but not beyond sixty-five (65) years which is hereby declared the compulsory retirement age, who has served at least five (5) years in the said establishment, may retire and shall be entitled to retirement pay equivalent to at least one-half (1/2) month salary for every year of service

key_points.label: half a month per year of service

question: How long can probationary employment last?
expected_answer: It shall not exceed six months from the date the employee started working, unless an apprenticeship agreement stipulates longer, under Labor Code Art. 296.

evidence.quote: Probationary employment shall not exceed six (6) months from the date the employee started working

question: On what grounds can a probationary employee be terminated?
expected_answer: For a just cause, or for failing to qualify as a regular employee under reasonable standards made known at the time of engagement, under Labor Code Art. 296.

evidence.quote: may be terminated for a just cause or when he fails to qualify as a regular employee in accordance with reasonable standards made known by the employer to the employee at the time of his engagement

key_points.label: failure to qualify under reasonable standards

question: What happens to an employee who is allowed to keep working after the probationary period?
expected_answer: The employee is considered a regular employee under Labor Code Art. 296.

evidence.quote: An employee who is allowed to work after a probationary period shall be considered a regular employee.

question: When does a casual employee become a regular employee?
expected_answer: After at least one year of service, continuous or broken, with respect to the activity in which the employee is employed, under Labor Code Art. 295.

evidence.quote: any employee who has rendered at least one year of service, whether such service is continuous or broken, shall be considered a regular employee with respect to the activity in which he is employed

question: What is an unjustly dismissed regular employee entitled to?
expected_answer: Reinstatement without loss of seniority rights and privileges, and full backwages inclusive of allowances and other benefits, under Labor Code Art. 294.

evidence.quote: entitled to reinstatement without loss of seniority rights and other privileges and to his full backwages

question: What are the just causes for terminating an employee?
expected_answer: Serious misconduct or willful disobedience, gross and habitual neglect of duties, fraud or willful breach of trust, commission of a crime or offense against the employer or the employer's immediate family or representatives, and analogous causes, under Labor Code Art. 297.

evidence.quote: Serious misconduct or willful disobedience
Gross and habitual neglect
Fraud or willful breach
Commission of a crime or offense
Other causes analogous

question: How much separation pay is due for redundancy, and what notice is required?
expected_answer: At least one month pay or one month pay for every year of service, whichever is higher, with written notice to the workers and the labor department at least one month before the intended date, under Labor Code Art. 298.

evidence.quote: separation pay equivalent to at least his one (1) month pay or to at least one (1) month pay for every year of service, whichever is higher
by serving a written notice on the workers and the Ministry of Labor and Employment at least one (1) month before the intended date thereof

key_points.label: one month pay per year of service
any_of: one (1) month pay for every year
one month pay for every year
one month's pay for every year
one month of pay for every year

common_mistakes: Using the half-month rate that applies to retrenchment

question: How much separation pay is due for retrenchment to prevent losses?
expected_answer: One month pay or at least one-half month pay for every year of service, whichever is higher, under Labor Code Art. 298.

evidence.quote: the separation pay shall be equivalent to one (1) month pay or at least one-half (1/2) month pay for every year of service, whichever is higher

key_points.label: half month per year of service

common_mistakes: Using the one-month rate that applies to redundancy

question: What separation pay is due when an employee is terminated because of disease?
expected_answer: At least one month salary or one-half month salary for every year of service, whichever is greater, a fraction of at least six months counting as one year, under Labor Code Art. 299.

evidence.quote: separation pay equivalent to at least one (1) month salary or to one-half (1/2) month salary for every year of service, whichever is greater

key_points.label: half month per year of service

question: How much notice must an employee give to resign without just cause?
expected_answer: Written notice at least one month in advance, under Labor Code Art. 300.

evidence.quote: by serving a written notice on the employer at least one (1) month in advance

question: When may an employee resign without serving any notice?
expected_answer: For serious insult on the employee's honor and person, inhuman and unbearable treatment, commission of a crime or offense against the employee or the employee's immediate family, and analogous causes, under Labor Code Art. 300(b).

evidence.quote: Serious insult by the employer or his representative
Inhuman and unbearable treatment
Commission of a crime or offense by the employer
Other causes analogous

question: For how long can a business suspend operations without terminating employment?
expected_answer: A bona fide suspension not exceeding six months does not terminate employment, under Labor Code Art. 301.

evidence.quote: The bona fide suspension of the operation of a business or undertaking for a period not exceeding six (6) months

question: Under the DOLE rules, how long must an employee be given to answer the first written notice in a just cause dismissal?
expected_answer: At least five calendar days from receipt of the notice, under DO-147-15, Rule I-A, Section 5.

evidence.quote: “Reasonable period” should be construed as a period of at least five (5) calendar days from receipt of the notice

question: Is a formal hearing always required before dismissing an employee for just cause?
expected_answer: No. Under DO-147-15, Rule I-A, Section 5, a formal hearing or conference becomes mandatory only when the employee requests it in writing, when substantial evidentiary disputes exist, or when a company rule or practice requires it.

evidence.quote: A formal hearing or conference becomes mandatory only when requested by the employee in writing or substantial evidentiary disputes exist or a company rule or practice requires it

common_mistakes: A formal hearing is always mandatory

question: What is the four-fold test for an employer-employee relationship?
expected_answer: Selection and engagement of the employee, payment of wages, power of dismissal, and power to control the employee's conduct, the control test being the most crucial, under DO-147-15, Rule I-A, Section 3.

evidence.quote: (1) the selection and engagement of the employee; (2) the payment of wages; (3) the power of dismissal; and (4) the power to control the employee's conduct

question: Can an employee be dismissed because of HIV status?
expected_answer: No. An employee shall not be terminated based on actual, perceived or suspected HIV status, under DO-147-15, Rule I-A, Section 6.

evidence.quote: An employee shall not be terminated from work based on actual, perceived or suspected HIV status.

question: What is the difference between just causes and authorized causes?
expected_answer: Just causes, under Labor Code Art. 297, are directly attributable to the fault or negligence of the employee. Authorized causes, under Labor Code Art. 298 and Art. 299, arise from business necessity, changing economic conditions and illness of the employee. See DO-147-15, Rule I-A, Section 4.

evidence.quote: These are causes directly attributable to the fault or negligence of the employee.
“Authorized Causes” refer to those instances enumerated under Articles 298 [Closure of Establishment and Reduction of Personnel] and 299

key_points.label: fault or negligence of the employee
authorized causes are in Arts. 298 and 299

question: What happens to a termination dispute before a Labor Arbiter can take the complaint?
expected_answer: It must go through mandatory conciliation-mediation, and no Labor Arbiter takes cognizance of an illegal dismissal complaint without a referral from the Desk Officer, under DO-147-15, Rule I-A, Sections 8 and 10.

evidence.quote: All disputes arising out of termination of employment shall be subject to mandatory conciliation-mediation
unless there is a referral from the Desk Officer

question: When do money claims from employer-employee relations prescribe?
expected_answer: Within three years from the time the cause of action accrued, under Labor Code Art. 306.

evidence.quote: shall be filed within three (3) years from the time the cause of action accrued

question: What are the prescriptive periods for offenses under the Labor Code and for unfair labor practices?
expected_answer: Offenses penalized under the Code prescribe in three years. Unfair labor practices must be filed within one year from accrual. See Labor Code Art. 305.

evidence.quote: Offenses penalized under this Code and the rules and regulations issued pursuant thereto shall prescribe in three (3) years.
All unfair labor practice arising from Book V shall be filed with the appropriate agency within one (1) year from accrual

key_points.label: one year for unfair labor practices

question: What is the substantial capital requirement for a contractor?
expected_answer: At least five million pesos, as paid-up capital for corporations, partnerships and cooperatives, or as net worth for a single proprietorship, under DO-174-17, Section 3.

evidence.quote: paid-up capital stock/shares at least Five Million Pesos (P5,000,000.00)

common_mistakes: P3 million, under the earlier rules

question: What is labor-only contracting and what is the consequence if it is found?
expected_answer: It is an arrangement where the contractor lacks substantial capital or investments and its employees perform activities directly related to the principal's main business, or where it does not control the work. The principal is then deemed the direct employer of the contractor's employees. See DO-174-17, Sections 5 and 7.

evidence.quote: not have substantial capital
directly related to the main business operation of the principal
does not exercise the right to control
the principal shall be deemed the direct employer

question: What happens if a contractor fails to register with DOLE?
expected_answer: Failure to register gives rise to the presumption that the contractor is engaged in labor-only contracting, under DO-174-17, Section 14.

evidence.quote: Failure to register shall give rise to the presumption that the contractor is engaged in labor-only contracting.

question: How much is the DOLE registration fee for a contractor?
expected_answer: One hundred thousand pesos, payable upon approval of the application, under DO-174-17, Section 19.

evidence.quote: Payment of registration fee of One Hundred Thousand Pesos (P100,000.00) shall be required upon approval of the application.

question: Is a principal liable when a contractor fails to pay its employees' wages?
expected_answer: Yes. The principal is jointly and severally liable with the contractor to the extent of the work performed, under Labor Code Art. 106, and is held responsible with the contractor for any violation of the Code under Labor Code Art. 109.

evidence.quote: the employer shall be jointly and severally liable with his contractor or subcontractor
every employer or indirect employer shall be held responsible with his contractor or subcontractor for any violation of any provision of this Code

question: Name arrangements that DOLE prohibits as illicit in addition to labor-only contracting.
expected_answer: They include farming out work to a Cabo, contracting through an in-house agency or an in-house cooperative, and contracting out by reason of an actual or imminent strike or lockout, under DO-174-17, Section 6.

evidence.quote: When the principal farms out work to a “Cabo”.
Contracting out of job or work through an in-house agency.
Contracting out of a job or work by reason of a strike or lockout whether actual or imminent.

question: Can an employer impose telecommuting on its employees?
expected_answer: It may offer telecommuting on a voluntary basis, or as a result of collective bargaining, on mutually agreed terms not less than the minimum labor standards, under DO-202-19, Section 3.

evidence.quote: may offer a telecommuting program to its employees on a voluntary basis or as a result of collective bargaining

question: How must telecommuting employees be treated compared with employees on the employer's premises?
expected_answer: They must get the same treatment as comparable employees at the employer's premises, and pay not lower than applicable laws or the CBA, under DO-202-19, Section 4.

evidence.quote: given the same treatment as that of comparable employees working at the employer's premises
Receive a rate of pay, including overtime and night shift differential, and other similar monetary benefits not lower than those provided in applicable laws

question: Must an employer tell DOLE that it adopted a telecommuting arrangement?
expected_answer: Yes. It must notify DOLE by submitting the prescribed report form to the nearest DOLE Field or Provincial Office, under DO-202-19, Section 7.

evidence.quote: The employer shall notify the DOLE on the adoption of a telecommuting work arrangement
to the nearest DOLE Field or Provincial Office

question: Can an employer require a woman employee to stay single?
expected_answer: No. It is unlawful to require as a condition of employment that a woman employee shall not get married, or to stipulate that she is deemed resigned upon marriage, under Labor Code Art. 134.

evidence.quote: It shall be unlawful for an employer to require as a condition of employment or continuation of employment that a woman employee shall not get married

question: Can an employer dismiss a woman because she is pregnant?
expected_answer: No. It is unlawful to discharge a woman on account of her pregnancy, or while on leave or in confinement due to her pregnancy, under Labor Code Art. 135.

evidence.quote: It shall be unlawful for any employer
To discharge such woman on account of her pregnancy, or while on leave or in confinement due to her pregnancy

question: Besides workers in the informal economy, who is covered by DOLE's guidelines on gender-based sexual harassment for such workers?
expected_answer: Kasambahay under the Domestic Workers Act, those in the informal economy, and those in establishments with ten or fewer employees, under DO-230-21, Part I, Section 1.

evidence.quote: Domestic Workers Act
Those employed in the informal economy
Those employed in establishments with ten or fewer employees.

question: How long must employment records be kept?
expected_answer: At least three years, in and about the premises of all workplaces unless a centralized recording system is implemented, under DO-183-17, Rule IV, Section 2.

evidence.quote: keep and maintain employment records in and about the premises of all workplaces for at least three (3) years

question: When may DOLE issue a Work Stoppage Order?
expected_answer: When non-compliance with occupational safety and health standards poses imminent danger to the health and safety of employees, under DO-183-17, Rule VIII, Section 1.

evidence.quote: when non-compliance with occupational safety and health standards poses imminent danger

question: Which establishments are the priority for routine labor inspection?
expected_answer: Those engaged in hazardous work, those employing children, those in contracting or subcontracting arrangements, and those employing ten or more employees, under DO-183-17, Rule V, Section 2.

evidence.quote: Those engaged in hazardous work
Those employing children
Those engaged in contracting or subcontracting arrangements
Those employing ten (10) or more employees

question: What happens if an establishment refuses an inspector access to records or premises?
expected_answer: It results in the filing of a criminal action against the responsible person or employer, under DO-183-17, Rule IX, Section 1.

evidence.quote: shall result in the filing of a criminal action

question: How is an employee who tests positive for dangerous drugs treated under DOLE rules?
expected_answer: The employee is dealt with administratively, under DO-53-03, Section F.

evidence.quote: Any officer or employee found positive for use of dangerous drugs shall be dealt with administratively

question: How far ahead must a notice of strike be filed for a bargaining deadlock and for unfair labor practice?
expected_answer: At least 30 days before the intended date for a bargaining deadlock, and 15 days for unfair labor practice, under Labor Code Art. 278.

evidence.quote: with the Ministry at least 30 days before the intended date thereof
In cases of unfair labor practice, the period of notice shall be 15 days

question: When must strike vote results be reported?
expected_answer: At least seven days before the intended strike or lockout, subject to the cooling-off period, under Labor Code Art. 278.

evidence.quote: furnish the Ministry the results of the voting at least seven days before the intended strike or lockout

question: How long is maternity leave for a private sector employee, and does Labor Code Art. 131 still govern it?
expected_answer: No. Labor Code Art. 131 was superseded by R.A. No. 11210 (2019), which gives 105 days, with an option to extend for 30 days without pay and 15 more days for solo mothers.

evidence.quote: Superseded by R.A. No. 11210 (2019), “An Act Increasing the Maternity Leave Period to One Hundred Five (105) Days for Female Workers With an Option to Extend for an Additional Thirty (30) Days Without Pay, and Granting an Additional Fifteen (15) Days for Solo Mothers

common_mistakes: Sixty days, from the old text

question: Do the Labor Code articles on househelpers still apply to domestic workers?
expected_answer: No. R.A. No. 10361, the Domestic Workers Act or Batas Kasambahay, expressly repealed Chapter III of Book III, including Labor Code Art. 139.

evidence.quote: All articles or provisions of Chapter III (Employment of Househelpers) of Presidential Decree No. 442, as amended and renumbered by Republic Act No. 10151, are hereby expressly repealed.

question: Does the Secretary of Labor still have power to arrest illegal recruiters under Labor Code Art. 38?
expected_answer: No. Paragraph (c) of Labor Code Art. 38 was declared unconstitutional by the Supreme Court in Salazar v. Achacoso.

evidence.quote: Article 38 par. (c) was declared unconstitutional by the Supreme Court in Salazar v. Achacoso

question: Is DO-198-18 still the current set of rules implementing the OSH law?
expected_answer: No. DO-198-18 was superseded by DO-252-25.

evidence.quote: This order was superseded by DO-252-25.

question: Which agency's law governs the training provisions of the Labor Code on manpower development?
expected_answer: Labor Code Art. 43 and the Title on manpower development were substantively modified and superseded by R.A. No. 7796, the TESDA Act of 1994.

evidence.quote: This Title was substantively modified and superseded by R.A. No. 7796, The TESDA Act of 1994
